newsitem.title: USA: ICG says Lucent not buying into it.
newsitem.headline: ICG says Lucent not buying into it.

text.p: ICG Communications does not see Lucent Technologies Inc taking an equity stake in it as a result of a seven-year $1 billion equipment deal announced on Tuesday, ICG chief executive J. Shelby Bryan said.
ICG is also not holding talks with ATT about being acquired, Bryan said in response to a quesiton.
ICG, which competes with regional Bell telephone companies, is buying Lucent's 5ESS-2000 switching system.
Bryan said ICG has about $500 million in cash, which will be adequate to cover the first part of the Lucent contract.
Denver-based ICG, which began offering service in Colorado in 1991, is also focusing on four other regions: California, the Ohio Valley, Texas and the Southeast.
Bryan said ICG's goal is to be the dominant number two phone service provider in the areas it is targetting. Most of its customer base is commercial.
Bryan said while ICG will assume the operational role, the relationship with Lucent is close. "We will rely heavily in certain aspects on Lucent," Bryan said.

ICG's strategy is to fous on identifying customer needs and deploying new services rather than use its resources writing software applications. "That must be done by others," Bryan said, because ICG does not have the economies of scale to tackle that task.
